text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Ministers Natan Sharansky and Yuli Edelstein to boycott cabinet.
- Sources: Iran, Hizbollah plan to hit Israeli, U.S. and Turkish targets.
- Israel wants France to broker Lebanon withdrawal.
- Ministerial hopes dim for former Justice Minister Yaacov Neeman. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: Coalition to thrive.
- Former Finance Minister Dan Meridor slams PM, Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel; says shekel-band decision caused serious economic damage.
- New shekel mechanism to increase arbitrage.
GLOBES
- Calm trading in foreign currency.
- Office Depot buys Super Office.
HAARETZ
- "Yisrael ba-Aliya": An extension for Netanyahu until Tuesday. In political establishment the chances of early elections are viewed as thin.
- Expectation is Ariel Sharon will be finance minister and Yaacov Neeman will not return to the government.
- Ultra-nationalist Yehuda Etzion, in ceremony filmed by Canadian TV, leads followers in sacrifice of lamb in preparation for building of a third Jewish Temple.
- War games carried out by Israeli army ahead of the 1982 Lebanon war showed chances of success were thin -- information was kept from Prime Minister Menachem Begin.
MAARIV
- Communications Minister Limor Livnat: "Furious." Netanyahu: "The coalition will hold its own."

- Gallup poll of Israeli Jews shows that if elections were held today 42 percent would vote for Labour's Ehud Barak and 33 percent for Netanyahu with 25 percent not knowing or refusing to say. But 47 percent believe government will run its term. Margin of error 4.5 percent.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Cabinet shuffle next week -- Sharon to finance ministry, Moshe Katzav to national infrastructure, Silvan Shalom to tourism and Michael Eitan to science.

- Dahaf poll of 504 Israelis show 51 percent believe there's a need to call early elections for prime minister in the wake of recent events, 45 percent say there's no need and 4 percent have no response. Poll has a 4 percent margin of error.
- Palestinian Authority prepares list of wanted Israelis who resort to violence.
